status: 工业场景美术探索，待用户选择，非正式资产
common_scene:
Use case: stylized-concept.
ONE finished THREE-PANEL INDUSTRIAL ART-DIRECTION COMPARISON BOARD for Zhouzhu, a playable third-person 3D game. Landscape 4:3, approximately 2048x1536; thin neutral ivory gutters. No writing, captions, numbers, symbols, logo, HUD or watermark.
ROLE OF INPUT IMAGE: STYLE AND CHARACTER REFERENCE ONLY. Keep its distinctive rendering language across ALL new panels. Replace the rural port with a genuinely MECHANIZED INDUSTRIAL PORT. Do not copy its scene composition or put another ordinary farmhouse in the foreground. The new scene is specified below.
THREE SHARED REQUIREMENTS: beautiful whole-scene composition, color and atmospheric depth; beautiful middle-distance character/machine/building shapes; beautiful close construction and material detail. All surfaces retain rich selective authored detail, never flat ground, generic primitives, photographic grunge or random ornamental clutter.
NEW FUNCTIONAL SCENE FOR BOTH STYLES:
A modest but clearly industrial SHIP-COMPONENT MANUFACTURING FACTORY and airship freight berth on a floating island. Cultural roots remain EAST ASIAN rural crafts evolving into industry. A 24m-long by 12m-wide manufacturing hall on the LEFT, approximately 6m wall/eave height: red-brown brick piers and infill, dark timber/iron structural frame, straight practical grey clay-tile roof with one narrow raised glazing band for daylight, rhythmic RECTANGULAR multi-pane windows, no cathedral arches or Victorian ornament. A broad open loading entrance and visible active work bays with machine tools. Repeated frame bays and overhead roof trusses are clear. This is industrial production, NOT an empty barn or warehouse. A small plain older rammed-earth timber house remains only at far left edge, showing continuity with the earlier settlement.
An understandable flow runs left-to-right: sorted metal bar stock and cast blanks at the input side, BELT-DRIVEN MACHINE TOOLS inside the hall, an inspection and assembly bench, identical finished cast-iron bearing housings/shaft brackets in crates at the loading door, one small FLATBED TROLLEY on a SHORT 15m ground-level rail run to the quay. No one carries heavy cargo over a long distance.
Machinery sample: one conventional compact metal-turning lathe with long bed, headstock/chuck, carriage and toolpost, tailstock, a stepped drive pulley; one upright drilling machine in the adjacent bay. Overhead LINE SHAFT supported by real bearing hangers; FLAT LEATHER BELTS connect individual line-shaft pulleys down to machine drive pulleys in comprehensible aligned loops. Only use pulleys/shafts/belts that transmit power to these machines. Primary power source is OUTSIDE THE FRAME AND UNDECIDED: no visible boiler, turbine, motor, electrical lighting, battery or power plant. Machines and industrial stage are provisional visual samples, not a historical setting declaration.
A simple functional straight-beam loading gantry at the quay with a small chain hoist transferring a crate from trolley to boat; restrained structural iron, wood where appropriate, few proper fasteners. No ornate crane tower or giant decorative cogwheels.
On the RIGHT one SAME modest 7.5m by 2.6m open cargo wooden SAILING AIRBOAT as in the style reference: single mast, plain cream rectangular battened sail, working rigging, a little more practical iron reinforcement at the gunwale, no balloon, engine exhaust, weapons, figurehead, wings or huge crystals. Whole mast and sail fit. Floatstone is hidden inside the hull, no magic effects. Short gangplank from quay, visible workable deck and cargo.
The yard has beautiful MATERIAL VARIETY and organized production: stone slabs at loading zone, compacted-earth approach with gravel and a few worn grass edges, dark wooden decks, grey iron, selective bronze/brass bushings, brown leather drive belts, hemp ropes, cloth covers and simple ceramic containers. Moderate use wear only at contact points; maintained machinery with interesting cast, forged and machined surfaces, not ruined, rusty everywhere or oil-soaked. Iron remains dark steel/iron, no gold-plated steampunk apparatus.
Same young adult East Asian boatman, about23, small practical black bun, plain faded INDIGO wrap-front hip-length work jacket, rolled sleeves, brown sash, undyed hemp cropped trousers, straw sandals, same identity as style reference. One adult workshop worker wears a simple indigo/earth-tone work jacket and plain brown apron, hair tied; practical ordinary clothes, no fancy costume or modern hardhat. Main panel has FOUR or FIVE adult workers/boatman total for scale, not a crowd.
Fair clear 10AM weather, sunlight from upper LEFT with open blue skylight. Both styles use equal light/weather/exposure. Cloud sea under the quay and three quiet distant vegetated floating rock islands. No waterfalls, big background city, extra airships, smoke/smog, night, sunset, cinematic godrays or magical/industrial spectacle.
EXACT BOARD LAYOUT:
TOP full-width upper58%: a wide playable HUMAN-EYE-HEIGHT view from the yard's approach; factory left and center, visible open machine bays/loading zone, short trolley track leading right to the simple gantry and small cargo airboat at island rim. Horizon around upper third of this panel. Human/door/machine/ship scales intelligible. Strong designed composition and rich ground/architecture, no aerial vista.
BOTTOM LEFT left48% of lower42%: a medium interior/threshold view of factory. Same young boatman and one workshop worker at the INSPECTION BENCH, looking at one finished shaft bracket; faces visible in three-quarter. Their hands rest with the measured part on the bench, no action hero pose. Behind them a recognizable lathe and one drill with aligned overhead line-shaft belt drive, roof trusses and repeated tall windows. Show faces, adult body shape, cloth fold construction, casting/machine silhouettes and workplace layout. Daylight only, no modern electric equipment.
BOTTOM RIGHT right52% of lower42%: an exquisitely composed CLOSE VIEW of a real functional SHAFT-BEARING ASSEMBLY from the same factory. Dark grey cast-iron split bearing housing bolted by four practical hex fasteners to a stout wood-and-iron bed; a steel shaft runs horizontally through it with a small bronze bushing rim visible, one plain dark-iron spoked FLAT-BELT pulley sits next to the bearing, and a correctly aligned brown leather belt wraps its rim and leaves the frame toward a drive pulley. A tiny simple lubrication cup at top, no labels or ornamental detailing. Include the edge of the timber mounting bed and one folded hemp wiping cloth; keep focus on the bearing/shaft/pulley connection and the contrast of CAST IRON, MACHINED STEEL, BRONZE, LEATHER, WOOD and CLOTH. Selective fine working marks, readable edge highlights, beautiful form, subtle local patina; calm areas between details. No exploded diagram, no random gears, no text, no incoherent disconnected gadget collage.
FAIR COMPARISON: the two boards have SAME machine types, layout, physical sizes, amount of goods, architectural construction and detail quality. Rendered forms, face design, painting, color relationships and shadow organization define the style difference. Do not make one more ornate, cleaner, larger or more spectacular. Both must feel like refined richly designed REAL-TIME THREE-DIMENSIONAL worlds with beauty from far to close, not a simple realism gradient.
World boundary: no magic apart from unshown floatstone; no energy runes, glowing stones, ornamental giant crystal, fantasy prop designs, sci-fi, European medieval styling, Japanese torii, exaggerated steampunk, extra decoration, game franchise characters or copied signature assets.

styles.name: 精绘日式三维
styles.prompt:
TARGET STYLE I1: Preserve and extend the REFINED HAND-PAINTED JAPANESE 3D RPG visual language of the reference, in the visual family of GRANBLUE FANTASY RELINK, now expressed through INDUSTRIAL FORMS. All three panels must be unmistakably detailed painterly 3D, not generic realistic machinery with an anime person pasted on.
Character has grounded elegant 7-head adult anime proportions, carefully drawn expressive eyes/brows and fine sculpted locks, simple working clothes. Facial form and cloth folds have fine selective drawn accents and nuanced painted half-tones.
Machine/building SHAPE DESIGN: elegant long controlled curves on cast supports, crisp rhythmic frame bays, compact readable pulleys and precise little fastener accents, clean but substantial modeled volumes, NO extra ornate curls. Surface detail is fine authored painting: long drawn grain following timber planes, delicately painted iron roughness and polished steel edge accents, nuanced blue-green reflected half-tones, leather edges and weave carefully selected, not photo microtexture or universal scratch noise.
Color and shading signature: luminous AZURE air and clear morning blue, jade/olive vegetation outside, warm CREAM and brick ochre light, chestnut timber, refined BLUE-VIOLET and turquoise cool reflections within iron shadows. Dark iron and small natural bronze highlights are materially convincing but richly colored. Every close surface is exquisite and detailed while shadows remain designed. Smooth painterly transitions, precise few contours at important joints, no heavy outline, no flat cell fields, no triangle mosaics.
Industrial architecture is as carefully drawn as the hero, material detail as beautiful as the overall vista. Keep factory scale modest and the work atmosphere ordinary. This style's identity is precise painted marks, flowing forms and luminous color, not ornate machinery or dense ornament.

styles.name: 成熟绘画式三维
styles.prompt:
TARGET STYLE I3: Preserve and extend the MATURE SCULPTURAL PAINTED-CG visual language of the reference, now through INDUSTRIAL FORMS. Bold coherent modeled planes with selective curves, rich opaque direction-following paint strokes, individualized ADULT humans. No generic photo-rendered factory or merely an oil-paint screen filter.
Character has 7.5-head mature adult proportions, strong individualized angular East Asian cheek/nose/brow planes, natural small deep-set eyes, calm attentive expression, capable working hands. Hair as a directional sculpted mass in a practical small bun, no anime fringe or glamorous model. Cloth folds organized in long angular rhythms with smaller painted seam accents.
Machine/building SHAPE DESIGN: cast iron housings have powerful simple plane-to-curve transitions, subtle irregular hand-worked edges, rhythmic regular factory piers/trusses, strong interesting but believable lathe/gantry silhouettes. Authored physical weight and manufacturing logic, not cartoon gadgetry.
Material language: visible controlled BROAD ACRYLIC/OIL-LIKE paint strokes, small beautifully designed marks at bolt heads, bearing seats, timber joints and leather edges; sculptural color-plane transitions, selective dry-brush/scumbling in rough cast texture, colored painted reflections across machined steel. Preserve all fine connection detail, but marks are authored rather than photographically noisy. Soft and hard edges deliberately varied.
Color and shading signature: warm GOLDEN OCHRE and BURNT SIENNA masonry/timber, cool STEEL-BLUE and muted PLUM half-tones on dark iron and in shadows, muted petrol/sage-green vegetation, ivory morning light and clear blue sky. The cool iron machinery and warm construction form a coherent sophisticated palette. Same ordinary 10AM weather, no sunset/neon/grimdark.
Every panel shares the expressive painted volumes, including the close bearing and belt. This style's identity is sculptural planes, mature faces and strong color relationships, not extra grime, damage, darkness, larger machines or a bigger industrial spectacle. No random faceted triangle patches, heavy outlines, watercolor paper or photoreal CGI.

Material language: visible controlled BROAD ACRYLIC/OIL-LIKE paint strokes, small beautifully designed marks at bolt heads, bearing seats, timber joints and leather edges; sculptural color-plane transitions, selective dry-brush/scumbling in rough cast texture, colored painted reflections across machined steel. Preserve all fine connection detail, but marks are authored rather than photographically noisy. Soft and hard edges deliberately varied.
Color and shading signature: warm GOLDEN OCHRE and BURNT SIENNA masonry/timber, cool STEEL-BLUE and muted PLUM half-tones on dark iron and in shadows, muted petrol/sage-green vegetation, ivory morning light and clear blue sky. The cool iron machinery and warm construction form a coherent sophisticated palette. Same ordinary 10AM weather, no sunset/neon/grimdark.
Every panel shares the expressive painted volumes, including the close bearing and belt. This style's identity is sculptural planes, mature faces and strong color relationships, not extra grime, damage, darkness, larger machines or a bigger industrial spectacle. No random faceted triangle patches, heavy outlines, watercolor paper or photoreal CGI.
